SF3 data is based on a sample population but totals have been extrapolated to coincide with whole population totals.

The spatial base for this data set was derived from Census TIGER line data based on RIGIS 1:5000 scale mapping accepted and updated by the US Census in 2005. It was spatially georeferenced into the Rhode Island State Plane Coordinate System by RIGIS in 2006 Tabular and Geographic US Census 2000 Summary File 3(SF3) information for general GIS use. The intention of this dataset was to provide an overview of data from summary file 3 (SF3). It does not include all data from SF3 only an overview of significant items. Users with more detailed needs may access additional source information, available from SF3, obtainable directly from the U.S. Census.

properties.snippet: Non-community wellhead protection areas in Rhode Island.
properties.description:
This hosted feature layer has been published in RI State Plane Feet NAD 83. 

A wellhead protection area (WHPA) is the portion of an aquifer through which groundwater moves to a well. Under the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (DEM) Wellhead Protection (WHP) Program approved by the US Environmental Protection Agency in 1990, DEM is responsible for delineating a WHPA for each of the public wells in the state. DEM contracted with the GZA Consulting to delineate select non-community stratified drift wells using analytical modeling and hydrogeologic mapping.

As of August 2013, the Rhode Island Department of Health Office of Drinking Water Quality (HEALTH) is responsible for delineating the Calculated Fixed Radius WHPA's for bedrock wells, based on the pump rate of the well. Non-Transient Non-Community Well - regularly serves at least 25 of the same persons (not residents) over 6 months of the year. Examples include wells serving schools and places of employment. Transient Non-Community Well - does not regularly serve the same persons, but does serve at least 25 people at least 60 days of hte year. DEM relied on technical input from the Wellhead Protection Program Advisory Committee in developing the delineation methodology. A mapping approach was required that was scientifically defensible, could be applied consistently across the state, and could be applied with the resources available to DEM. The delineations are based on reasonably available information regarding the hydrogeologic environment and the well characteristics. The WHPAs were delineated using the US Geological Survey quadrangle maps at a scale of 1:24000. 

WHPA maps are available for review at the DEM Office of Water Resources, on the DEM web page at www.dem.ri.gov/maps, and on the Rhode Island Geographic Information System webpage at www.rigis.org.

candidates.title: Rhode Island Statewide Current Land Use

properties.snippet: Generalized current land use data for Rhode Island derived from municipal and statewide datasets, supporting planning and land management.
properties.description:
Overview

This feature service provides a comprehensive dataset representing the generalized Current Land Use across the state of Rhode Island. It integrates data submitted by multiple municipalities along with the state's Land Use Land Cover dataset to create a unified land use dataset consistent with statewide criteria.

Feature Layer

  • PLAN_Statewide_CLU: This layer contains the Current Land Use data representing various land use categories statewide. It includes data contributed by numerous municipalities including: Bristol, Central Falls, Charlestown, Coventry, Foster, Hopkinton, Jamestown, Johnston, Lincoln, Little Compton, Newport, North Providence, North Smithfield, Pawtucket, Portsmouth, South Kingstown, Tiverton, Warren, West Greenwich, and West Warwick. For municipalities not providing their own data, the 2020 Land Use Land Cover data from the Rhode Island Geographic Information System (RIGIS) was generalized to fit the state's land use classification scheme. The dataset represents polygon features characterized by land use categories and descriptions, providing a valuable resource for planning and land management.

Geographic Coverage

This dataset covers the entire state of Rhode Island with detailed municipal-level land use information.

Use Cases

  • State and municipal planning efforts
  • Environmental and land development assessments
  • Resource management and policy making

Data Sources and Licensing

The data was collected through a combination of municipal contributions and RIGIS datasets, employing both automated and manual photointerpretation processes. The dataset is provided under the RIGIS license agreement with specific terms regarding data accuracy and usage. Users are advised to consider source and accuracy information for responsible application, and to acknowledge RIGIS and municipal contributors in derived products.

Supporting Documents

StoryMap: Rhode Island Land Use 2050 Data Services

For a more detailed analysis and description of the methodology used in this project, please see the following technical papers available at planning.ri.gov:  
-  Technical Paper 170 - Data Collection Methodology  and
-  Technical Paper 171 - Land Use Change and Suitability Study.

properties.snippet: These data provide available contemporary high-resolution national shoreline for Rhode Island.
properties.description:
This hosted feature layer has been published in RI State Plane Feet NAD 83.

Accuracy is variable depending on source. This shoreline is not to be used for legal purpose since it includes shoreline compilation with less stringent data acquisition requirements and quality control measures as compared to the National shoreline.

Shoreline is a dynamic interface between land and water. The cartographic depiction of shoreline is a representation at the time of survey. Continually Updated Shoreline Product (CUSP) provides the most up-to-date shoreline of the United States and its territories. CUSP will identify the most up-to-date surveys for inclusion, employ state-of-the-art technology for cartographic review, attribute shoreline features, and develop a strategy to replace shoreline as it becomes available. CUSP is a separate product from the project-based national shoreline mapped by the National Geodetic Survey (NGS). The national shoreline from the Coastal Mapping Program provides accurate tidal referenced shoreline, aids to navigation, hazards to navigation, and associated cultural and topographic reference data primarily for nautical chart applications. CUSP will only include shoreline and alongshore features that represent shoreline (groin, breakwater, and jetty). CUSP has less stringent data acquisition requirements and quality control measures compared to the Coastal Mapping Program's National Shoreline. Where applicable, CUSP will reference a mean high water shoreline based on vertical (VDatum) modeling or image interpretation using water level stations and/or shoreline indicators. CUSP is built upon contemporary NGS's National Shoreline which comprises approximately one-third of our nation's shoreline and focuses primarily on the most navigational significant areas. CUSP uses and incorporates both NOAA and non-NOAA contemporary sources (Lidar, imagery, and external shoreline vectors) to replace shoreline areas of older vintage. Shoreline continues to be reviewed with contemporary imagery and additional data is being included with the goal of providing a continuous shoreline of our nation and its territories. For additional information, please see the CUSP One Pager.

properties.snippet: A detailed statewide vector dataset depicting Rhode Island's 2020 land use and land cover conditions developed through orthoimagery interpretation and employing an updated Anderson Level III classification. Created under the direction of the RI Department of Administration, RI Division of Statewide Planning
properties.description:
Overview

This feature service provides a comprehensive, statewide geospatial dataset representing the land use and land cover conditions as of 2020 for Rhode Island and its immediate surrounding areas. The dataset extends slightly into neighboring states Connecticut and Massachusetts to the extent of available aerial orthoimagery.

This hosted feature layer has been published in RI State Plane Feet NAD 83.

Dataset Origin and Methodology

The dataset was developed through a combination of automated and manual photointerpretation methods, comparing high-resolution 2020 leaf-off aerial orthoimagery against 2011 imagery to detect and delineate changes over the nine-year interval. The derived data represents a seamless vector map with a minimum mapping unit of 0.5 acres.

Classification System

The land use and land cover classes are based on the Rhode Island modified Anderson Level III classification scheme, consistent with previous datasets from 1988 through 2011, but updated with the addition of two new categories for renewable energy infrastructure: ground-mounted solar energy systems and wind energy systems. Notably, marinas were reclassified from transportation and developed recreation categories to commercial to enhance classification accuracy.

Layer Description

  • Land Cover and Use 2020: This primary feature layer details land use and land cover polygons with attributes including classification codes, descriptive categories, acreage, and symbology categories. It includes varied land cover types ranging from forest, wetlands, developed areas, and agricultural fields, to specialized classes reflecting recent energy developments.

Geographic and Thematic Coverage

While focused on Rhode Island, this dataset also covers adjacent regions. The dataset is vital for urban planning, environmental management, resource conservation, and infrastructure development projects.

Data Use Considerations

The dataset should be used with awareness of its preliminary planning purpose, as it does not encompass all wetlands known from other RIGIS sources.  Wetland areas previously classified as forested wetlands are depicted as forest areas in this dataset. Users are advised to consider spatial and attribute accuracy, along with classification nuances, when integrating this data into analytical workflows. Statistical comparisons with RIGIS land use and land cover data prior to 2003 should be treated with caution since some differences in the methodologies used to delineate features were employed.

Licensing and Attribution

The data is shared under the Rhode Island Geographic Information System (RIGIS) license agreement. Users must acknowledge RIGIS and primary data contributors in derivative products and comply with the usage terms detailed in the licensing agreement.
